description: A TS.MADD item that back-fills an already-closed bucket recalculates that bucket from the source as it stood when the item would have been applied sequentially: RTS applies items one at a time in argument order, each item above the running maximum appending and each item at or below it back-filling, with the retention trim running between items. So the recalculation sees the window implied by the running maximum at that item's position -- which drops a sample an earlier item in the same batch pushed out of retention. Appends are unaffected: a bucket closed by an append still publishes the value it accumulated, including a sample the trim evicts immediately afterwards. Merging the batch as one sorted run against the pre-batch last timestamp erases both halves -- on a series the batch itself populates every item outranks `prev_last`, so nothing is recognised as a back-fill and the expired sample stays folded into the bucket (sum reports 6 where RTS reports 1).
